key_insight: Large-eddy simulations show that lateral channel constriction can trigger plunging flows in bedrock rivers, with the strongest plunging occurring at about 35% constriction under lower flows and about 50% under higher flows.
engineering_relevance: These results help improve bedrock incision and landscape evolution models by capturing the unsteady, high-shear dynamics that drive localized erosion in constriction-pool-widening channels.
method: Eddy-resolving large-eddy simulation (LES) of laboratory-scale bedrock river flow
Parametric testing of different channel constriction levels under lower and higher discharge conditions
Analysis of velocity inversion, shear stress, velocity variance, and flow intermittency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports LES results across varying constriction and flow conditions, identifying optimal constriction ranges and showing increased shear stress and intermittent plunging at higher discharge.
watch_item: The findings are based on laboratory-scale simulations, so field-scale geometry, sediment interactions, and scaling effects may limit direct transfer to natural rivers.
paper_title: Large Eddy Simulation of Plunging Flows in Laboratory-Scale Bedrock Rivers
